assign.request: Second-pass UX review of /imagine/mag/: five sentences, try an alternative layout for real and measure it, make it more visual, verify persistence, check paging-vocabulary integration, land.
steps: build alternative layout for real, measure at 1280/3440

log.msg: task opened for realm mag — read readme, page.js, contents/page.js, Article.js, mag.css, issue.json, doc/decisions.md, and the paging vocabulary readme/words.js. mag is mature: a 2026-09-04 cold-read pass already fixed the standfirst copy and the cover veil. Persistence (baseline() with a custom saved: message) is already wired in contents/page.js — my job is to verify it, not just confirm the import.

assign.now: alternative layout tested and reverted; building the visual fix

log.msg: BEFORE shots taken (shots/before-1280.jpg, before-3440.jpg) before any edit: the cover fills the full row at 100% width, 0 dead space, no scroll -- already better than the sitewide 46%-used finding because it is width:full, not a large-capped column.

ALTERNATIVE tried: disabled both golden-share :has() rules in mag.css (temp comment-out, restored -- git diff was empty before continuing) so the cover's plain full/min-width:100% governed the click into contents, testing the paging-vocabulary bullet honestly (launch/takeover vs the bespoke recede). Measured at 1280: the row auto-scrolled 421px to reveal contents, decapitating the masthead mid-word (T/Co sliced off at the viewport edge, shots/alt-takeover-test-1280.jpg). At 3440 it ate 504px of the poster's own left inset (shots/alt-takeover-test-3440.jpg). REVERTED -- confirmed by measurement, not by trusting the code's own comment, that the golden share is a necessary override.

VISUAL fix built and kept: coverlines. The cover named its topic but never showed what was inside -- added page.js coverlines() listing the six real article titles (from issue.json) under the CTA, numbered in the same --prim accent the entries/bars already use. Cover-only (.mag-cover.active-ancestor .mag-cover-lines{display:none}), so it never touches the golden-share numbers. No height cost measured at 1280/720, 1280/800, 3440/1440 (scrollHeight===clientHeight all three).

PAGING VOCABULARY checked honestly: opening the issue and moving between articles is core's launch throughout (a real child column) -- not invented. What IS bespoke and unnamed in that vocabulary is the cover's own three-CSS-state shrink (full -> 38.2% -> 20%). Added one line to readme.md Watch-out saying so and linking /imagine/paging/, plus a decisions.md entry, rather than leaving it silently undocumented.

PERSISTENCE verified live, not just import-read: headless run (ui-test/reading-marks-saved.png, reset-clears.png) opened two articles, confirmed 1 of 6 -> 2 of 6 read reactively, confirmed the green Saved-in-this-browser mark with its custom message renders, confirmed count AND the green mark both survive a hard reload, clicked Reset, confirmed 0 of 6 and the mark disappears, confirmed that ALSO survives reload. Zero console errors across the whole run.

BUG found and fixed (not just the known .md-extension trap): /imagine/mag/doc/ 404'd outright because doc was never in the cover's children: array, so readme.md's and decisions.md's links to each other left the app for raw markdown (confirmed by clicking: page.url ended in .md, no .page element). Root cause matches /imagine/paging/doc/page.js's own history. Fix: added mag/doc/page.js (route(), not children:, one record) copying paging's exact recipe, and added "doc" to mag/page.js's children (routing-only -- column() renders no child links itself). Clicked the full readme<->decisions round trip headless afterward: resolves in-app both ways, title updates, zero new console errors at 1280 and 3440 (one PRE-EXISTING sitewide readme/page.js probe 404 remains, reproduced on /imagine/paging/readme/ too -- not introduced by this task, not this realm's finding, out of fence to fix).

FIVE SENTENCES before: what=a poster cover for a small magazine (The Column, Issue 01) with a headline, a teaser line, and one button. use=click Open the issue, the only clickable target. goal=recognise it as a real magazine's cover and want to open it. hard=1/5, obvious at a glance, nothing to parse. better=it names its own topic but stays silent on what is actually inside -- a real cover previews its contents before you commit to opening it.

FIVE SENTENCES after: what=the same poster cover, now also showing the six real pieces inside it before you click. use=click Open the issue (or the poster itself) to launch the contents beside it, then click any piece, or a coverline title, to know what is coming. goal=trust that six worthwhile pieces are actually inside, then get into the contents. hard=1/5, same one-click simplicity, the coverlines are read not operated. better=let each coverline jump straight to its article (skip the contents column for a returning reader who already knows which piece they want), and a second issue so the contents-remembers-you mechanism has more than one issue's worth of history to prove itself against.

links.label: The cover -- coverlines added, golden share kept

assign.outcome: **Kept the golden-share layout, added coverlines, fixed a real doc-routing bug.** The cover already avoids the sitewide dead-space problem (it is `width: "full"`, not `large` — 100% width used, 0px dead band, before and after). Tried the paging-vocabulary alternative for real (plain `full`/takeover instead of the bespoke 38.2%/20% recede) and reverted it with numbers: at 1280 it decapitated the masthead mid-word, at 3440 it ate 504px of the poster's own inset. Kept and built: **coverlines** — the six real article titles now show under the CTA before you click, a fourth typographic tier answering the cover's silence about what's inside; cover-only, zero height cost, measured. Verified persistence live (not just import-read): the read count and the green 'Saved in this browser' mark both update reactively, survive reload, and Reset clears both, also across reload. Found and fixed a real bug beyond the known .md-link trap: `/imagine/mag/doc/` 404'd outright because `doc` was never in the cover's `children:`, so readme.md and decisions.md's own cross-links left the app for raw markdown — added `doc/page.js` (route(), copying `/imagine/paging/doc/`'s exact fix) and declared `doc` as a routing-only child. Named the paging vocabulary honestly in the readme: every hop here is core's `launch`; the cover's own recede has no name in that vocabulary and now says so, linking `/imagine/paging/`. Zero console errors at 1280/3440 on every page touched beyond one pre-existing sitewide `readme/page.js` probe 404 (also on `/imagine/paging/readme/`, not this task's to fix).
